name: 12_chunk_multibyte_loses_nothing
why: Real transcripts are full of em dashes, accents, CJK and emoji, and this is where the two languages legitimately differ: Go cuts on UTF-8 byte boundaries (hardSplitRunes) while Python cuts on code points. Boundaries may differ; LOSS may not. A byte cut in the middle of a rune would corrupt the record and is what hardSplitRunes exists to prevent.

not_compared.chunk_count: Different UNITS, both correct: the Go limit is 24000 BYTES (len() on a Go string counts bytes) and the Python limit is 24000 CODE POINTS. On multibyte text the same limit therefore yields a different number of chunks. Neither loses data - rejoined_sha256 above is the proof - and both stay under their own limit. Aligning the units would change record sizes in production for no integrity gain.
not_compared.max_chunk_size: Same reason: bytes on the Go side, code points on the Python side.

on_failure: rejoined_sha256 different from input_sha256 means bytes were lost or a rune was cut in half; a corrupted record is worse than a missing one because nothing flags it. Check hardSplitRunes (core.go) or the slice loop in split_into_chunks (hermes-agent/transcript.py).
